findings.claim: The route's fix-base write (absent .round = another round) overwrites test-gate-route.sh's fixture snapshot on G1/G2/G3 (round-1/2 fix-batch in docs/work/t), so G6, G7, G22 lose their fix hunks; the plan forbids editing existing cases.
findings.closure: Closure: a fix-base with no fix-base.round beside it is kept (snapshot wrote it); the route writes only when fix-base is absent or fix-base.round holds another round; a G case after a fixture snapshot routes a round-1 fix-batch with output kept and fix-base byte-identical; G32/G35 use their own slug.

findings.claim: kept keys only on the round number; a fresh /loop:review restarts at round 1 and would keep a stale fix-base.round=1 base from an earlier review.
findings.closure: Closure: a round-1 fix-batch always writes when fix-base.round exists (round 1 never reads the scope); kept applies to round >= 2 with a matching .round, and to a fix-base with no .round (Q1); G33's rerun case is at round 2; a G case with .round=1 left by a cleared review and a new round-1 fix-batch outputs written.

findings.claim: The Python head allowance's only name check misses star imports, trailing statements on the line, and pytest module-level names (pytestmark, setup_module, pytest_*), each able to neutralise every frozen case.
findings.closure: Closure: the contract refuses *, any text after the statement on its line except a # comment, and a binding named pytestmark, pytest_plugins, setup_module, teardown_module, setup_function, teardown_function, setUpModule, tearDownModule or any pytest_*; PI cases deny from x import *, import os; g = 1, from h import pytestmark and from h import setup_module with a verdict.

findings.claim: No PI case covers auto + unfreeze verdict with the file not listed in .tdd-unfrozen (rows mode off, reachable: rows come from verdicts only when the file is listed); PI1 and PI2 test the same state.
findings.closure: Closure: a PI case runs lp_py_project, empties .claude/.tdd-unfrozen, sets an auto record with one unfreeze verdict, and the head insertion passes; PI1 is renamed to the listed file in rows mode.

findings.claim: arbiter.md:50-51 says imports go import-first or in one Edit with the case body; the Python contract accepts head alone or head + new case, not head + a rewrite of the unfrozen case (TS AM49 form); PK62 does not force the Python wording.
findings.closure: Closure: PK62 requires the Python sentence to say the Python freeze takes the imports in their own Edit (or with a new case), and keeps 'in one Edit with it' scoped to TypeScript.

findings.claim: The spec wants each skeleton to name the allowed values of mode, status, dimension, kind, p1_class; only dimension is pinned.
Contract (b) asks on -u/-a whatever the tracked state while the spec says a stash with no tracked change passes as today (open question 2).

The freeze-side readers of listed ids (tdd_py_lib.py:561 unfrozen_ids, tdd-freeze-tests.sh:200) still accept uppercase only; a moi line '# b204:' is accepted by protect-files but ignored by the freeze.
The new deny catches any new non-verbatim # line (a plain header comment too), and in moi replaces the guarded ask; '#<line>' with no space is unsettled.
Option-skipping subcommand detection differs from git/kit_stash (args[0] else push); combined short flags (-qu) and long abbreviations (--incl) are not named.
Vigilance omits PK50 ('import a frozen test case needs', in test-writer.md:145) and docs/Claude_Workflows.md:168 listing stash asks.
G44 in docs/work/v interacts with G23/G43 refusals there (a round-1 skeleton now writes fix-base into v).
